openIssues: [TILES-OWNED, ROOT CAUSE, worst] Normals lifted to EXACTLY the horizon get zero diffuse from an overhead sun, so every vertical face is ambient-only and ambient is near zero. One defect, five symptoms: (a) lamps-close-12.png — the lamp post shaft is near-black navy over most of its length with an abrupt light/dark band partway down (the seam between vertices that were lifted and vertices that were already above horizon); (b) tree-close-12.png at tod 12 — the whole forest_entrance_front canopy is dark teal, only silhouette-edge leaves catch light, at NOON; (c) tree-close-12.png — 2-4px pure-BLACK vertical streaks run top-to-bottom through the canopy at x approx 205/400/470/690/930/1150 (trunk side faces and edge-on cards); (d) catalog-12.png — bench_s and the hedge underside read as dark navy blobs; (e) lamps-17.5.png — all four posts and shades go dark purple with only the sun-facing sliver lit. FIX: lift affected normals to a minimum elevation of ~15-25 degrees above horizon, or re-derive them from face geometry. 'To the horizon and no further' trades a black silhouette for a black shaft. This is what makes the tree read as cardboard next to docs/refs/01-forest-tilemap-frame.png.

[TILES-OWNED] tree-close-12.png, top-centre: a lawn-coloured diamond punches through the middle of the canopy. ki02c is a flat horizontal slice, so materialGeometryRoles gives it flatOnly:true; combined with SOFT alpha that makes it decal:true in makeMaterial (src/tiles/materials.js:198), which sets depthWrite:false plus a ground polygonOffset — on a canopy 3m in the air. A canopy slice that writes no depth occludes nothing behind it, so ground shows through wherever no other opaque leaf card covers. The decal rule needs a height or category guard so it only catches slices lying ON the ground (kage_out/h_kage), not canopy slices.

[TILES-OWNED] No contact shadow or ambient occlusion anywhere at noon. hedge-close-12.png: the hedge and its stone kerb meet the lawn with zero darkening — the hedge looks pasted on, not planted. ground-12.png: the path/grass boundary has no occlusion either. openIssues: THE SUN SHADOW MAP DEGENERATES INTO A CASTER-LESS FRAME-WIDE SLAB AT EXACTLY THE LOW-SUN HOURS (07:00, 08:00, 17:30) -- defect #4's core complaint, unfixed. Measured on the same lawn pixel (high-street framing, x=60 y=250) with and without --envNoShadow: tod 7 -> 95/95, tod 8 -> 111/35, tod 9 -> a correct house-shaped wedge, tod 12 -> 119/119, tod 17.5 -> 100/28. That is NOT monotone in sun altitude, and a caster shadow can only lengthen as the sun drops, so this is not a caster shadow. crops/diff-sm-hs-7.png (17.09% of pixels), crops/diff-sm-hs-8.png (13.90%) and crops/diff-shadowmap-hs-17.5.png (28.71%) contain only huge straight-edged trapezoids and full-width bands with no building, roof, awning, bench or lamp silhouette; crops/diff-sm-hs-21.png and crops/sw-9.png contain correct ones. First place to look: src/environment/index.js:346-348 -- `normalBias = 0.026 + 0.055*graze*graze` and `bias = -0.0005 - 0.0006*graze` -- the shadow map's behaviour is not monotone in graze. Confirm by shooting --tod 8 with normalBias pinned to the tod-9 value; if the slab becomes a house shadow, that curve is the cause. (Note --envNoShadow costs 235 -> 150 draw calls, so it removes the whole pass, not just the map.)

OVERLAPPING SHADOWS MULTIPLY TO LITERAL BLACK. castShadows.js blends `blendSrc: DstColorFactor, blendDst: ZeroFactor` -- a pure multiply -- on top of the shadow map's own multiply, so two shadows compound rather than take a min. Golden-hour plaza paving inside a stacked shadow measures rgb(0,0,10) against lit paving rgb(151,99,76); every sprite's ink outline goes to exactly (0,0,0) (crops/mask-black-17.5.png). Ref 04 golden hour has 0.00% pure-black pixels and only 0.06% below L=8; ours are 2.47% and 9.24%. Clamp the combined shadow to the authored shadowMul floor instead of letting two multiplies stack.

NIGHT CRUSHES 7.58% OF THE FRAME TO EXACTLY (0,0,0) -- ref 03 is 0.88%, r2 was 4.29%. crops/mask-black-21.png shows it is structural, not incidental: the whole shaded facet of every roof, the alley between the two buildings, and the lawn west of the townhouses (grass sample there reads rgb(1,1,1)). Defect #1's 'hue crushed out' is only half fixed -- lit regions keep hue, shaded regions have no value left to carry any. Ref 03 gets its depth from a wide value range inside saturated colour (meanSat 0.854, lumP1 1.2, P99 158.4); ours gets it by clipping (meanSat 0.647). Give the night fill a non-zero floor per channel.

SPRITES ARE NOT GROUNDED AT NOON. The planar projection's length goes to zero as the sun rises, so at 12:00 --envNoCast changes only 0.56% of pixels and the sole grounding left is a contact blob so weak it is invisible at 1:1 (crops/snivy-12.png: the Snivy has a faint mauve smudge under it and nothing else). Every trainer and Pokemon reads as a sticker on the paving. Ref 03's Poochyena carry a hard dark shadow even directly beneath them. Floor the projected run so it never collapses below a compact ellipse, or restore a stronger contact blob under the projection.

SPRITE CAST SHADOWS READ AS SMUDGES, NOT SILHOUETTES. `uSoft` ramps to 0.9 + 1.9 = 2.8 atlas texels across a 5-tap cross, then `smoothstep(0.18, 0.66)` -- at 17:30 crops/diff-nocast-17.5.png shows featureless horizontal lozenges with holes in them where a Pokemon should be recognisable. Ref 03's Poochyena shadow keeps ears and legs. Cut uSoft by ~3x at the feet and let the widening do the work, or tighten the smoothstep window.

GOLDEN HOUR IS UNDER-EXPOSED AGAINST THE REFERENCE, and got darker this round. meanVal 0.377, lumP50 51.9, lumP1 0.0 against ref 04's 0.530 / 64.2 / 26.3. Ref 04 is a hot, luminous, fully-lifted frame with nothing crushed; ours reads as dusk. r2 measured 0.447 -- this is a regression, and r2's city-17.5.png is the better picture of the two.

BROAD HORIZONTAL LIGHT/DARK BANDING ACROSS THE LAWN at 07:00, 08:00 and 17:30 (crops/sw-7.png, sw-8.png, sw-17.5.png) that survives --envNoShadow at tod 7, so it is a terrain/tile lighting seam rather than a shadow. It reads as corduroy stripes on the grass and is the single most 'programmer art' thing in the daytime frames.

A HAIRLINE PURE-BLACK STROKE TRACES THE BOUNDARY OF EVERY SHADOW THAT IS CORRECT. Visible on the house shadow in crops/sw-9.png and around the townhouse shadow in crops/nwh-21.png -- a 1 px depth-test seam where the comparison flips. It announces the shadow as a rendering artifact rather than as light.

NO RIM OR KICKER ON ANY SPRITE AT ANY HOUR. crops/nighttrainer-21.png: the trainer stands beside a lit lamp, takes the pool's warmth uniformly across his whole card, and has no moon-side edge and no lamp-side edge. Ref 03's Poochyena and its flowers both carry a bright top-lit face against the dark. A cheap alpha-edge kicker driven off the key direction would buy more than anything else on this list at night.

AT GOLDEN HOUR THE SUN-FACING ROOF FACET TAKES A FLAT SATURATED ORANGE THAT OVERRIDES THE MATERIAL'S OWN ALBEDO. On the NW townhouse in hs-17.5.png the left facet is pure orange while the roof plane beside it is brick brown, split by a razor seam with no gradient -- the roof reads as two decals, not one lit form. The main roof plane meanwhile barely moves between 08:00 (216,86,55) and 17:30 (216,70,24), so the dominant surface reads unlit while the small facet reads over-lit.

LAMP POSTS READ AS DESATURATED STICKS WITH NO LIT/SHADE SIDE, AND ARE OVER-BRIGHT AT NIGHT. Shaft pixel at (679,340): rgb(165,147,136) at 08:00, rgb(117,80,67) at 17:30 -- a dull brown-grey while the path beside it is a saturated warm orange (crops/hslamp-17.5.png) -- and rgb(205,165,131) at 21:00, which makes a 2 m post the brightest large surface in the night frame after the bulbs themselves and reads as self-illuminated.

openIssues: [tiles-owned, but it wrecks every simulation frame - flag it, don't chase it] Every meadow tree has a bright vertical stripe rammed through it from canopy to root. Cropped at 6x from c-wide-tod175.png (region 980,440-1120,680): the canopy renders as a face-on quad while a SECOND quad is seen edge-on as a full-height 1-texel column, and the two receive completely different light - at 17:30 the canopy is blood-red while the stripe stays bright green. Same artifact at noon (c-tod12 at ~1400,560: a brown lintel-like slab with a black wedge above the canopy). The only <=4-cell tree models in bw2-adastra are `tree`, `round_tree`, `darker_pine`, all 2x2 'billboard' - so the crossed-quad geometry or its per-face normals are wrong in the tile models. Fix belongs to tiles (single camera-facing quad, or DoubleSide with an up-flattened normal). Simulation's only mitigation is to stop planting them until it's fixed.

[sim-owned] The meadow ground is a literal 50/50 checkerboard. `buildWalkMap` fills with `tiles.pick(tiles.find(SLUG,{category:'ground',tags:['grass']}), cx, cz, {salt:11})` - and that query returns exactly TWO models: `grass` (tags flat/floor/grass) and `grass_v2` (tags flat/floor/grass/**raised**). So half the map is randomly set to a raised, differently-valued tile, producing the two-tone speckle and the hard horizontal value seams visible across c-tod12, c-tod08 and the crop behind the Lillipup. tiles' own ov-12.png shows organic mottled grass, so this is simulation's fill query, not the tileset. Fix: fill with `grass` only, or drop `grass_v2` to a low-probability accent (<10%) rather than a coin flip.

[sim-owned] The `grass` mode fails its own stated purpose - the lead is swallowed. In c-grass-tod08.png only the top ~30% of Oshawott's head clears the tall grass at (650,530); the mode exists to show 'the lead has stepped into the tall grass while the trainer is still on the path' and you cannot see the lead. The tileset ships `grass_patch_half` and `grass_decoration` alongside `tall_grass`, but buildWalkMap takes `tall[0]`. Fix: use the half-height model at the patch rim, or move the freeze cell to a ragged edge cell, or raise the actor so >=50% of the lead reads above the blades.

[environment-owned] Hard grey rectangular shadow slabs cross the road at 08:00, 17:30 and 21:00. In c-tod175.png there are straight horizontal bands at y~180, ~570 and ~740 with dead-straight top edges that stair-step once; the 4x crop (580,400-900,600) shows they are a flat uniform grey that DESATURATES what it crosses instead of darkening it warmly. They are not tree-shaped and no caster is visible. At golden hour a shadow must carry the ambient's colour - compare docs/refs/04-cave-golden-hour.png where shadowed rock stays warm. Fix belongs to environment (shadow bias/cascade + coloured ambient in shadow).

[sim-owned] The `city` mode fails its own stated purpose - the queue is invisible in the crowd. In c-city-tod21.png I cannot tell the party from the extras: the four members are scattered among ~12 city NPCs at similar scale, with lamp-head props bisecting several sprites. The mode's point is 'the party walking a real map somebody else authored'. Fix: pull the camera to the empty half of the square, freeze on a step where the bend is unobstructed, or temporarily clear the lobby NPCs from the queue's read.

[sim-owned] The `wide` mode makes the subject unreadable. At k=1 (c-wide-tod175.png) the four walkers are ~30 px tall blobs at (700-810, 440-640) and the shape of the queue - the entire stated point of the showcase - cannot be resolved. Either raise k to ~1.5, or keep k=1 but frame the corner tighter so the line occupies more than 4% of the frame height.

[pokemon-owned, flag it] The trainer's back sprite is an unreadable blob at this camera pitch. Cropped at 5x from c-tod12 (700,380-900,580): a black-and-orange oval occupies ~55% of the sprite's height with no distinguishable shoulders, arms or legs beneath it - just a lavender mass, a stray orange rectangle and a pink stub. Next to it in c-grass-tod08 the Snivy and Tepig profiles read cleanly, which is the comparison that damns it. Against docs/refs/01-forest-tilemap-frame.png, where the BW trainer's cap/body/legs separate at a fraction of this zoom, this is the weakest asset in frame.

[pokemon/sim] The party is not anchored to the light at low sun. `src/pokemon/field.js:106` sets `castShadow = false` and relies on the contact blob. At 17:30 the trees throw 6-tile directional shadows while the 4x crop of the party shows essentially nothing under either walker - they read as pasted on. docs/refs/03-forest-voxel-night.png keeps a soft directional shadow trailing each follower even at night. Either strengthen and stretch the blob with sun azimuth (field.js:245 claims to do this - it is not visible) or let sprites cast into the shadow map.

[sim-owned] The `run` mode does not read as running. I pixel-diffed the party strip (560,380-900,900) between c-tod12.png and c-run-tod12.png: 61,671 of 176,800 px differ, so a distinct run frame IS being drawn - the side-by-side crop shows a wider stride and a swung arm. Either freeze the run at a mid-air/extended-stride tick, add a speed cue, or drop the mode - as shot it proves nothing a critic can judge.

But at the `plaza` framing the six in-frame lamps produce no discernible pool on the paving - the whole square is a uniform flat brown at 21:00 (n21-plaza.png) - while the high-street pair clearly does (n21-highstreet.png). Determine whether environment's 8-nearest PointLight cap (acknowledged at layout.js:219-221) is spending its slots on off-screen lamps, or whether intensity 1.25 / radius 13 is simply too weak against the plaza material. Also: the plaza lamp heads render pale WHITE on screen, not the 0xffb166 sodium the code specifies, so the glow quad is not taking the lamp's colour.

THE 'STONE-PAVED SQUARE' IS UNTEXTURED MUD [city]. It is the largest surface in every plaza shot and it is flat, smeared brown with no paving pattern, no joints and no border course. Worse, at close range it is visibly bilinear-soft while every other surface in frame is crisp nearest-filtered (n12-close.png) - a filtering/material mismatch that breaks the pixel grid the refs hold rigidly. PLAZA_STONE exists in layout but is not reading as stone at any distance.

THE POKE MART IS VISUALLY A COPY OF THE POKEMON CENTER [asset, not mapping]. Checked: structures/pack.json ships three genuinely distinct models (house_a 5x4, poke_mart 6x5, pokemon_center 8x6) and plotModel (layout.js:53) resolves each by its own subcategory - the mapping is correct. The problem is the assets: both shops carry the SAME red hipped roof, the SAME beige wall, the SAME red/white awning and the SAME Pokeball roof sign (n12-plaza.png, n12-highstreet.png, budget-1080-noon.png). Nothing says 'Mart'. In n12-wide.png the whole town is a six-building red-roof monoculture. Re-author or re-tint the mart roof (blue is the series convention) and give it its own sign.

GRASS TILES AS A VISIBLE CHECKERBOARD [terrain/tiles]. Every lawn shows a perfect grid of alternating light/dark green squares - unmissable in n12-pond.png, n12-garden.png and n12-southgate.png. Variance is alternating on cell parity instead of hashing on position. Note the tiles showcase grass (docs/progress/_boot/sc-tiles.png) is smooth and organic with no checkerboard, so this is introduced by the city map or its biome preset, not inherent to the tileset.

TREES RENDER NEAR-BLACK AT EVERY HOUR [tiles/props material]. The tree line is a black-to-navy silhouette with bright orange trunk flares at the base. At noon a tree cannot be black. The left third of n12-garden.png is a solid black void; same in n12-pokecenter.png and n12-pond.png. The trunk material lights correctly and the canopy does not, so it is specific to the foliage planes - normals facing away, or unlit vertex colours.

HARD BLACK SHADOW SLABS AND LAWN BANDING AT NIGHT AND LOW SUN [environment]. n21-pokecenter.png has a razor-straight black wedge across the left grass with no occluder. n21-wide.png throws 20-tile hard black streaks from every tree at 21:00 with the sun below the horizon, and shows a rectangular tonal boundary in the lawn at the shadow-camera extent. g175-wide.png bands the entire meadow in horizontal light/dark stripes. Reference 03-forest-voxel-night.png keeps its night shadowing soft and subtle.

BENCHES, HEDGE TUBS AND FLOWER BEDS DO NOT READ AS OBJECTS [city]. At close range a bench is a flat dark rectangle that looks like a floor grate (n12-close.png). Hedge tubs are bare green cubes with pink dots placed in perfectly uniform rows of five with zero rotation or spacing variance. Flower beds are flat decals lying on mud at a finer pixel scale than everything around them. The scalloped green edging ribbon repeats identically along every lawn edge and reads as a caterpillar (n12-southgate.png).

GOLDEN HOUR IS A FLAT ORANGE WASH AND NIGHT BLOOM BLOWS OUT [environment grade/post]. g175-wide.png collapses grass, roofs and roads onto one hue with no value separation; reference 04-cave-golden-hour.png keeps full structure under its orange. At night the shop windows bloom to pure white with no detail left (n21-pokecenter.png) where reference 03 keeps bloom restrained enough to preserve the light source's shape.

__HOOKS__.focus(cx,cz) IS DEAD FOR THE CITY SHOWCASE [city/main]. `--focus 50,20` produced the plaza framing, pixel-identical in composition to `--preset plaza` (n12-pond-focus.png). simulation re-centres the rig on the trainer every frame and focus() only sets the rig without teleporting; preset() works because focusOn() teleports first. index.js:56-60 documents exactly this failure mode for presets but left the harness hook with it. Any gauntlet or critic run using --focus silently gets the default view.

PROPS ON THE OPEN LAWN READ AS LITTER [city]. The barrels, log, woodpile and axe sit on bare grass east of the Mart with nothing tying them to the town - four unrelated objects with no fence, no yard, no path (n12-mart.png, right side). Group them against a wall or inside an enclosure so they read as a woodyard rather than scatter.

STAGING: EVERY HUMAN IN THE CAST FACES AWAY FROM THE LENS [city/npcs]. The trainer and both NPC people are posed facing north, the same way the camera looks, so no face ever reads - at distance the back of a white cap over red hair reads as a featureless blank head (n12-close.png, n12-plaza.png). coreRequests.want: a `tileset` field on Placement (or a multi-tileset MapDraft), so terrain.load can realise a map that mixes bw2-adastra with structures and props
coreRequests.why: `tiles.buildInstances(scene, slug, placements)` resolves modelId against one tileset, so a structures id put through an AdAstra draft silently draws an unrelated AdAstra model. Every scene that places an authored building has to build and dispose its own extra InstancedWorlds (src/city/structures.js). It works and costs 21 draw calls, but it is a trap every future map author will fall into once (DECISIONS #26a).

coreRequests.want: environment.lamps.add({ point:false }) — a glow-only bulb that never claims a slot in the 8-light pool
coreRequests.why: lamps.update() hands the pool to the eight bulbs nearest the camera focus, by distance alone. A lit window wants a glow quad and a small wall wash; a street lamp wants the ground pool. Today registering more than a couple of windows near the camera silently takes the PointLights away from the street lamps, so the city registers exactly two lit doorways and no window bulbs at all.
coreRequests.closedBy: environment r2 - lamps.add({ point:false }) exists and is verified in the running page (a point:false bulb at the camera focus claims no PointLight; a normal bulb two cells away takes env:lamp0; the pool stays at 8). Not yet CALLED by any scene, so city still has to pass the flag for its windows before the frame changes. DECISIONS #31h.

coreRequests.why: Both render as a pale grey blob roughly a third of a cell across with a blue rim, although their catalog record claims a 1x1x0.86 bush with the plant sprite on it. Reproduces with nothing else in frame at /?showcase=preview&mode=props&filter=hedge. They are the only two greenery props in the set, so the city plants AdAstra's hedge1 instead. assets/props + tools/assets are not city's to edit (DECISIONS #26e).

coreRequests.want: environment: a readable dusk between golden hour and night
coreRequests.why: tod 19.1 (environment's own 'dusk' preset) already renders as dark as tod 21.5; the last light in the sky is gone by 18.5. docs/progress/city/r1/golden.png (17.3) and dusk.png (19.1) are two hours apart and look like different scenes; dusk.png and night.png are 2.4 hours apart and look identical. The lamp ramp is fine — it is the sky and the key that fall off a cliff.
coreRequests.closedBy: environment r2 - the dusk keyframes were rebuilt and the day/night key floor unified; DECISIONS #31g

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: freeze the film-grain phase when config.timeFrozen is set, as environment already freezes its lamp flicker
coreRequests.why: DECISIONS #14 promises the same URL gives the same pixels, and the harness sets timeFrozen=1 for exactly that. Everything else obeys it: two runs of ?showcase=city&tod=21.5 put every sprite, lamp and shadow on the same pixel, but the grain reseeds and the PNGs differ by up to 6/255 on every pixel. With &grain=0 they are byte-identical. It costs a round-trip diff between two rounds its whole meaning.

coreRequests.want: environment: an ambient/exposure floor at night and a fill that does not take the sun's tint at full strength
coreRequests.why: tod 21 renders every tile the same navy-black and tod 17.5 renders every tile the same orange - docs/progress/tiles/r2/catalog-21.png and lamps-17.5.png. docs/refs/03 keeps a warm dirt path, green grass and readable flowers at night and docs/refs/04 keeps rock/sand/shadow separation under a warm key. tiles' own materials, normals and emissives are verified correct at noon in the same shots; nothing tiles can do to a material survives a fill that is both near-zero and monochrome.

coreRequests.want: environment: turn the shadow-casting sun off below the horizon, and lengthen the shadow as it sets
coreRequests.why: docs/progress/tiles/r2/lamps-17.5.png (sun low, shadows should be long) has almost no shadow; lamps-21.png (sun below the horizon, shadows should be gone) has long hard jet-black diagonals from every lamp. The light has flipped sides after sunset and is still casting.

coreRequests.want: a placement yaw that is not a quarter turn, or an exporter pass that splays a crossed-billboard prop's two cards
coreRequests.why: Every AdAstra tree is two upright cards at x=1 and z=1 and the camera never yaws (ARCHITECTURE 2.7), so the x=1 card is permanently perpendicular to the view and rasterises as a full-height sliver of canopy texture. `simulation` measured the same geometry independently (DECISIONS #29) and plants no tree at all because of it. Placement carries `rot: 0|1|2|3` only (ARCHITECTURE 7), so tiles cannot rotate a tree off the camera axis without breaking the one-tile-one-cell grid contract, and assets/ + tools/ are not tiles' to edit. Round 2's normal floor stops the sliver being black, but it is still a sliver.

coreRequests.want: for the integrator: simulation's `variety: 0` showcase workaround (DECISIONS #29) can be retired
coreRequests.why: It was added because the per-cell UV phase tore AdAstra's 4x4 global grass pattern at every cell edge. tiles round 2 phases a globally-mapped tile by its own 4x4 block instead, so the pattern stays continuous inside a block and only the repeat is broken - measured in docs/progress/tiles/r2/hedge-close-12.png at 3x the game zoom and ground-12.png at mid distance. simulation should re-shoot with the workaround removed before it is deleted.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: expose the shadow softness. `PCFSoftShadowMap` has a fixed kernel and `light.shadow.radius` is ignored by it; a VSM or a PCSS tap count that environment could set per hour would let a low sun have a soft penumbra and a noon sun a hard one.
coreRequests.why: Round 2 fixed a shadow's depth and colour (it carries the fill's hue instead of going to black) but not its edge, and every shadow in the game is still a razor line at 2048/56 = 0.027 world units per texel. docs/refs/01 and 03 both show soft-edged shadows. This is the last visible gap between our frame and theirs, and the type of shadow map is core's.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: read `config.shadowNormalBias` / `config.shadowBias` every frame in makeSunShadow.update(), instead of only at construction.
coreRequests.why: A grazing sun needs a much bigger normal offset than an overhead one. environment already computes the per-hour value and writes it straight onto `three.sun.light.shadow`, which works, but it means the config keys are decorative and a second writer (the debug overlay, a future tuner) would be silently overridden.

coreRequests.want: tiles: call `environment.lamps.add()` from the tiles showcase's `lamps` and `catalog` modes.
coreRequests.why: tiles-lamps-21.png shows four street lamps whose glass blooms and whose ground is untouched, and that frame was cited by two critics as 'a lit lamp casts no light pool'. The pool is real and demonstrable in the city (ab-pool-21.png) - tiles' own stage simply never registers a bulb, so environment has nothing to light. One call per lamp cell, the same three lines src/environment/showcase.js already uses.

coreRequests.want: tiles: the 22-degree normal floor can be relaxed now, and should be re-measured rather than removed.
coreRequests.why: DECISIONS #30a clamps every normal to 22 deg above the horizon because a vertical face took hemisphere fill only. Round 2 added two directional fills: an anti-sun `bounce` at 20 deg (a wall turned away from the key takes 0.94 of it) and a camera-axis `camFill` at 38 deg. A vertical face now has two real sources with direction, which is the condition the clamp was working around. ab-fills-off-8.png against city-8.png is the measurement of what the fills are worth on exactly those surfaces.

coreRequests.want: a rim/Fresnel term the environment can drive - either a shared material onBeforeCompile hook every module's materials pass through, or a rim pass in core/render.js's composite driven from the depth/normal buffers it already renders
coreRequests.why: Round 3's ranked note 4 is 'night away from lamps has no accent - it needs a rim/specular term on silhouettes' (docs/refs/03 sells its whole night on rim light along the fence posts). Every material in the frame is a MeshLambertMaterial owned by tiles and pokemon, and Lambert has no view-dependent term at all: no light I can add from environment produces a rim, because a back light gives a camera-facing card dot(N,L) < 0. This is the last defect in the night frame that environment cannot reach from its own folder.

coreRequests.want: expose shadow.radius / a PCF radius on the sun light, or switch the shadow map type per preset
coreRequests.why: core sets PCFSoftShadowMap in makeRenderer and its filter width is fixed, so tile and building shadows have a constant penumbra whatever the sun's elevation and whatever the distance from the contact point. The critic's note 3 asks for the opposite ('shrink the PCF radius near the contact point'). The projected sprite shadows in src/environment/castShadows.js do contact-harden, which makes the mismatch between the two shadow kinds visible in the same frame.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js should read config.shadowBias and config.shadowNormalBias every frame instead of once in makeSunShadow
coreRequests.why: environment recomputes both from the sun's elevation every apply() (a grazing sun needs roughly three times the normal offset a noon sun does) and has to write them straight onto three.sun.light.shadow to make them take effect. That works but it means two owners for the same two numbers.
